Algebra I · Lesson 6.2

Conversion Factors

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A conversion factor is a ratio of one amount to itself written in two units, so it is worth 11. One gallon and four quarts are the same volume, so 4 qt1 gal1 gal4 qt​ has equal volumes above and below the bar. Multiplying by it is multiplying by 11, which changes the unit and not the amount. The first two problems give the fraction.

Problem
A fuel tank holds 46 gallons, and 1 gal=4 qt1 gal=4 qt. Multiply 46 gal46 gal by 4 qt1 gal1 gal4 qt​, writing the unit inside the fraction so that gal above the bar cancels against gal below it. Enter the tank's capacity in quarts.
Show a hint
  • Write 46 gal46 gal as 46 gal1146 gal​, so gal sits above the bar in the amount and below the bar in the factor.
  • Once gal cancels, what is left is 46×446×4 with qt as the only unit remaining.
Show the full solution
Cancelling gal above against gal below leaves 46×446×4 quarts, so the capacity is 184184​. A quart is smaller than a gallon, so more of them cover the same volume, and 184184 is larger than 4646 as it has to be.
Problem
A second tank on the same lot holds 268 quarts. The same fact 1 gal=4 qt1 gal=4 qt also gives the factor 1 gal4 qt4 qt1 gal​, which has qt below the bar. Multiply by that factor and enter this tank's capacity in gallons.
Show a hint
  • Write the tank as 268 qt11268 qt​, so qt is above the bar. It cancels only against a factor with qt below the bar.
  • After qt cancels, the arithmetic left is 268÷4268÷4 and gal is the only unit remaining.
Show the full solution
Cancelling qt above against qt below leaves 268÷4268÷4 gallons, so the capacity is 6767​. The two factors are one fact written two ways, and which one to use depends on which unit has to cancel.
Key idea
A conversion factor is worth 11. Divide both sides of 1 ft=12 in1 ft=12 in by 1 ft1 ft and the left side becomes 11, so 1=12 in1 ft1=1 ft12 in​. Divide the same equality by 12 in12 in instead and 1=1 ft12 in1=12 in1 ft​. So every stated equality between two units gives two fractions, each worth 11, and each the other turned upside down. Multiplying an amount by either one multiplies it by 11, which leaves the amount alone and changes only the unit it is written in.
Problem
A pallet of bolts weighs 592 ounces, and 1 lb=16 oz1 lb=16 oz. The two factors available are 16 oz1 lb1 lb16 oz​ and 1 lb16 oz16 oz1 lb​, and only one of them cancels the ounces. Enter the weight in pounds.
Show a hint
  • Write the weight as 592 oz11592 oz​, so oz is above the bar. Only a factor with oz below the bar cancels it.
  • A pound is heavier than an ounce, so the number of pounds is smaller than 592592. Multiplying by 1616 cannot be right.
Show the full solution
The factor with oz below the bar is 1 lb16 oz16 oz1 lb​, and cancelling oz leaves 592÷16592÷16, so the weight in pounds is 3737​. The other choice gives 94729472 and leaves the label oz2lblboz2​, which is not a weight.
Problem
A recording runs 1020 seconds, and 1 min=60 s1 min=60 s. A student multiplies 1020 s1020 s by 60 s1 min1 min60 s​ and reports that the recording is 61200 minutes long. Enter the correct length in minutes.
Show a hint
  • Check the units in the student's product. Multiplying 1020 s1020 s by a factor with s on top gives s times s, so nothing cancels and the label left over is s2minmins2​.
  • The s in 1020 s1020 s cancels only against an s on the bottom. The fact 1 min=60 s1 min=60 s also gives the factor 1 min60 s60 s1 min​, which has s there.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by 1 min60 s60 s1 min​ cancels s and leaves 1020÷601020÷60, so the length in minutes is 1717​. The student used the reciprocal factor, so the result is 36003600 times too large, and the leftover label s2minmins2​ is not a time.
Key idea
Units cancel like common factors. Write the unit symbol inside the fraction and treat it as one more factor in the product. A unit above the bar and the same unit below divide out exactly as the 77 does in 5×73×73×75×7​, and the units that remain are the units of the result. The choice between the two forms is then settled by which unit has to cancel, not by remembering whether to multiply or divide. Put the unwanted unit below the bar and the wanted unit above it.

Not every pair of units has a fact stated directly between them. Sometimes one fact runs from the starting unit to a middle unit, and a second fact runs from that middle unit to the one wanted. The next two problems take that route, the first through one middle unit and the second through two.

Problem
A gym orders 8 coils of climbing rope, with 1 coil=30 m1 coil=30 m and 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm. Neither fact is a direct coil-to-centimeter conversion. Multiply the 8 coils by two conversion factors in a row and enter the total length in centimeters.
Show a hint
  • The unit meters is common to both given facts, so the chain is coils to meters to centimeters, one factor for each step.
  • The chain is 8 coils×30 m1 coil×100 cm1 m8 coils×1 coil30 m​×1 m100 cm​, with coil below the bar in the first factor and m below the bar in the second.
Show the full solution
Cancelling coils gives 8×30=2408×30=240 meters, and cancelling meters gives 240×100240×100, so the length in centimeters is 2400024000​. Both factors equal 11, so the two together equal 11 as well, and the rope has the same length as before, only measured in a smaller unit.
Problem
A recipe is written in cups and the jug in the kitchen is marked in milliliters. Use 1 cup=16 tablespoons1 cup=16 tablespoons, 1 tablespoon=3 teaspoons1 tablespoon=3 teaspoons and 1 teaspoon=5 mL1 teaspoon=5 mL. Enter the volume of 6 cups in milliliters.
Show a hint
  • Three stated facts give three factors, run in the order cups to tablespoons to teaspoons to milliliters, and each factor carries the unit you already have below the bar so that unit cancels.
  • Tablespoons and teaspoons are both intermediate units and both cancel, and what is left is 6×16×3×56×16×3×5.
Show the full solution
Cancelling cups, then tablespoons, then teaspoons leaves 6×16×3×56×16×3×5, so the volume in milliliters is 14401440​. Multiplying the three factors together first gives 16×3×5=24016×3×5=240, so the whole chain is the single factor 240 mL1 cup1 cup240 mL​, and any number of cups then takes one step.
Key idea
Chains of conversion factors. Multiplying by several factors in a row converts an amount through intermediate units. Write each factor so the unit just produced is below the bar, and stop when only the wanted unit remains. Each factor is worth 11, so their product is worth 11 and the amount is unchanged however many factors it takes. Counts named by ordinary nouns cancel the same way, since 1 coil=30 m1 coil=30 m is an equality between two descriptions of one length just as 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm is.

A rate is written with one unit above the bar and a different one below, so it carries two units at once. The next problems change both of them. Speeds, flow rates and rates of pay all have this shape, and a pace written as time over distance is the same information as a speed written as distance over time.

Problem
A conveyor belt runs at 48 meters per minute. Use 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm and 1 min=60 s1 min=60 s. Both units change, so two factors are needed. Enter the speed in centimeters per second.
Show a hint
  • Write the speed as 48 m1 min1 min48 m​. The m to be removed sits above the bar and the min to be removed sits below it, so the two factors go in the opposite way up from each other.
  • The chain is 48 m1 min×100 cm1 m×1 min60 s1 min48 m​×1 m100 cm​×60 s1 min​.
Show the full solution
Cancelling m above against m below and min below against min above leaves 48×100606048×100​, so the speed in centimeters per second is 8080​. The minutes factor goes in as 1 min60 s60 s1 min​ and not the other way up, since the min to be removed starts below the bar and cancels against a copy above it.
Fun fact
In 1793 France fixed the meter as one ten-millionth of the distance from the equator to the pole along the meridian through Paris. Delambre and Mechain spent seven years surveying that arc to set the length.
Problem
A runner's watch reports a pace of 3 minutes 45 seconds per kilometer, which is 225 s1 km1 km225 s​. Use 1 h=3600 s1 h=3600 s. Enter the speed in kilometers per hour.
Show a hint
  • The unit asked for has km above the bar and h below it, so the pace's s has to cancel and an h has to arrive, and the one fact available for both is 1 h=3600 s1 h=3600 s.
  • Turned over the pace is 1 km225 s225 s1 km​, and multiplying that by 3600 s1 h1 h3600 s​ cancels s and leaves km above the bar with h below it.
Show the full solution
Turning the pace over gives 1 km225 s225 s1 km​, and multiplying by 3600 s1 h1 h3600 s​ cancels s and leaves 3600÷2253600÷225, so the speed in kilometers per hour is 1616​. Turning a rate over states the same information with the two quantities exchanged, and 16×225=360016×225=3600 checks it, since sixteen kilometers at 225225 seconds each take exactly one hour.
Key idea
Converting a rate changes two units at once. A rate is a fraction with unlike units above and below the bar, so multiplying by one factor changes one of them and leaves the other. Two are needed. The top unit cancels against a copy of itself below the bar of one factor, and the bottom unit against a copy above the bar of the other, so the two factors are written the opposite way up. Turning a rate over exchanges the two quantities without changing the information, so a pace in time per distance and a speed in distance per time are one fact written two ways.

An area is a length times a length, so converting an area means converting both lengths, and the same factor is used twice. Write 1 yd21 yd2 as 1 yd×1 yd1 yd×1 yd and replace each yard on its own. A volume is three lengths multiplied, so the same factor is used three times.

Problem
A patio covers 34 square yards, and 1 yd=3 ft1 yd=3 ft. One square yard is 1 yd×1 yd1 yd×1 yd, so convert each of the two lengths and see how many square feet one square yard holds. Enter the patio's area in square feet.
Show a hint
  • A square yard is a square measuring 3 ft along each side, so count the square feet inside one of them first.
  • One square yard is 3×3=93×3=9 square feet, so the factor is 9 ft21 yd21 yd29 ft2​.
Show the full solution
One square yard is 3 ft×3 ft=9 ft23 ft×3 ft=9 ft2, so the factor is 9 ft21 yd21 yd29 ft2​ and the area is 34×9=30634×9=306​. Using the length factor once gives 102102 and leaves the label yd⋅ftyd⋅ft, since only one of the two lengths was converted.
Problem
A shipping crate has a volume of 5 cubic feet, and 1 ft=12 in1 ft=12 in. Enter the crate's volume in cubic inches.
Show a hint
  • One cubic foot is a cube whose edges each measure 1212 inches, so converting the edge length alone is not enough.
  • One cubic foot is 12×12×12=172812×12×12=1728 cubic inches.
Show the full solution
One cubic foot is a cube with 1212-inch edges, so it is 12×12×12=172812×12×12=1728 cubic inches, and the volume is 5×1728=86405×1728=8640​. Using the conversion factor of 1212 once gives 6060 and twice gives 720720, but a volume is three lengths multiplied together, so the factor belongs in the product three times.
Key idea
Squared and cubed units. A square unit is one length multiplied by a length equal to it. Replace each of those two lengths by the kk smaller units it equals and the product becomes k×kk×k of the smaller square unit, so the numeric factor is used once per length and ends up squared. A cubic unit is a product of three lengths, so the same replacement leaves k×k×kk×k×k. Written as factors, an area is multiplied by the conversion factor twice and a volume three times, which is why an area conversion is never just kk.

A conversion factor can be built from any stated equality between two amounts, and the two amounts need not be the same kind of thing. A price, a rate of pay, and a count per container are all equalities of that kind, so each one has two factors, and the choice between them comes down to the unit that has to cancel.

Problem
A field technician is paid 35 dollars per hour and works 6 hours per shift. Each of those statements gives a conversion factor, one between hours and dollars and one between shifts and hours. Enter the pay in dollars for 8 shifts.
Show a hint
  • Start from 8 shifts and pick the factor that cancels shifts, which leaves hours.
  • The chain is 8 shifts×6 hours1 shift×35 dollars1 hour8 shifts×1 shift6 hours​×1 hour35 dollars​.
Show the full solution
Cancelling shifts and then hours leaves 8×6×358×6×35, so the pay in dollars is 16801680​. Shifts and hours are both units of time, while dollars and hours are not, and nothing about the method changes, since 35 dollars per hour states that one hour of work goes with 35 dollars the way one foot goes with 12 inches.
Problem
A trading post prices goods in four measures, with 1 varn=7 sedge1 varn=7 sedge, 1 sedge=3 pell1 sedge=3 pell and 5 pell=2 quill5 pell=2 quill. The last fact has no 11 on either side. A merchant holds 15 varn. Enter the value in quill.
Show a hint
  • Three facts and three factors. Take varn to sedge, sedge to pell, then pell to quill, each one written with the unit you are getting rid of below the bar.
  • 15×7=10515×7=105 sedge, then 105×3=315105×3=315 pell. Only one orientation of the last factor cancels pell, so use that one.
Show the full solution
Chaining 15 varn×7 sedge1 varn×3 pell1 sedge×2 quill5 pell15 varn×1 varn7 sedge​×1 sedge3 pell​×5 pell2 quill​ cancels varn, sedge and pell in turn and leaves 15×7×3×25515×7×3×2​, so the value in quill is 126126​. Using the last factor upside down gives 315×52=787.5315×25​=787.5, with pell uncancelled and no quill in the answer.

Every conversion here was a multiplication by a fraction worth 11, chosen so the unwanted unit appeared above the bar and below it, and in the area and volume cases the same factor was used twice or three times. Lesson 6.3, Percents, uses a ratio whose second part is always 100100. The question there is what an amount is being compared against.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A sack of rice has a mass of 9000 grams, and 1 kg=1000 g1 kg=1000 g. Enter the mass in kilograms.
Show the solution
Multiplying by 1 kg1000 g1000 g1 kg​ cancels the grams and gives 9000100010009000​, so the mass in kilograms is 99​. The other fraction, 1000 g1 kg1 kg1000 g​, also equals 11, but it gives 90000009000000 with units of g2kgkgg2​, which is not a mass.
Practice
A spool carries 4500 centimeters of thread, and 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm. Enter the length of the thread in meters.
Show the solution
Cancelling cm leaves 4500÷1004500÷100, so the length in meters is 4545​. A meter is longer than a centimeter, so the count of meters is the smaller number.
Practice
A bench is 156 inches long, and 1 ft=12 in1 ft=12 in. Multiplying by 12 in1 ft1 ft12 in​ gives 18721872, a number far larger than the length in inches, and leaves the label in2ftftin2​. Pick the factor that cancels inches instead and enter the length in feet.
Show the solution
Multiplying by 1 ft12 in12 in1 ft​ cancels the inches and leaves 156÷12156÷12, so the length in feet is 1313​. The student's factor has inches above the bar as well, so nothing cancels and the label on 18721872 is in2ftftin2​, not feet.
Practice
A bakery counts its rolls in dozens and has 51 dozen, with 1 dozen=12 rolls1 dozen=12 rolls. Multiply by a conversion factor that cancels dozen, and enter the number of rolls.
Show the solution
The factor 12 rolls1 dozen1 dozen12 rolls​ cancels dozen, so the number of rolls is 51×12=61251×12=612​. The flipped factor 1 dozen12 rolls12 rolls1 dozen​ would leave 51÷1251÷12, which is why dozen belongs in the denominator.
Practice
A stationery order is 12 boxes, where 1 box=20 packs1 box=20 packs and 1 pack=50 envelopes1 pack=50 envelopes. Enter the number of envelopes in the order.
Show the solution
Writing 12 boxes×20 packs1 box×50 envelopes1 pack12 boxes×1 box20 packs​×1 pack50 envelopes​ and cancelling boxes and then packs leaves 12×20×5012×20×50, so the number of envelopes is 1200012000​. Each box holds 20×50=100020×50=1000 envelopes, so the order is 12×100012×1000, a quick check on the size.
Practice
A warehouse holds 8400 bottles, packed at 1 case=12 bottles1 case=12 bottles and 1 pallet=25 cases1 pallet=25 cases. Enter the number of full pallets.
Show the solution
Cancelling bottles and then cases leaves 840012×25=840030012×258400​=3008400​, so the number of full pallets is 2828​. Both factors go in with the old unit underneath, 1 case12 bottles12 bottles1 case​ and then 1 pallet25 cases25 cases1 pallet​, which is the same order the two facts are written in.
Practice
A delivery is 9 crates, with 1 crate=6 trays1 crate=6 trays, 1 tray=8 punnets1 tray=8 punnets and 1 punnet=15 berries1 punnet=15 berries. Enter the number of berries.
Show the solution
Cancelling crates, trays and punnets in turn leaves 9×6×8×159×6×8×15, so the number of berries is 64806480​. Each of the three factors is worth 11, so the delivery is the same size either way and only the thing being counted is different.
Practice
A tap fills a tank at 12 liters per minute, and 1 h=60 min1 h=60 min. Enter the fill rate in liters per hour.
Show the solution
Multiplying by 60 min1 h1 h60 min​ cancels the min and gives 12×6012×60, so the rate in liters per hour is 720720​. Dividing by 6060 instead gives 0.20.2, which is the wrong direction, since more liters come out in an hour than in a minute.
Practice
A snail moves 3 centimeters per second. Use 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm and 1 h=3600 s1 h=3600 s. Enter the speed in meters per hour.
Show the solution
3 cm1 s×1 m100 cm×3600 s1 h1 s3 cm​×100 cm1 m​×1 h3600 s​ cancels cm and s and leaves 3×36001001003×3600​, so the speed in meters per hour is 108108​. Each conversion factor is a fraction equal to 11, so multiplying by it changes the units and not the speed.
Practice
A conveyor carries 900 kilograms per hour. Use 1 kg=1000 g1 kg=1000 g and 1 h=60 min1 h=60 min. Enter the rate in grams per minute.
Show the solution
Cancelling kg and h leaves 900×10006060900×1000​, so the rate in grams per minute is 1500015000​. The hours factor goes in as 1 h60 min60 min1 h​ rather than 60 min1 h1 h60 min​, since the h below the bar cancels only against an h above it.
Practice
A courtyard covers 7 square meters, and 1 m=100 cm1 m=100 cm. Enter the area in square centimeters.
Show the solution
One square meter is 100 cm×100 cm=10000 cm2100 cm×100 cm=10000 cm2, so the area is 7×10000=700007×10000=70000​. Converting only one of the two lengths gives 700700, which is too small by a factor of 100100.
Practice
A poster covers 4320 square inches. Use 1 ft=12 in1 ft=12 in. Enter the area in square feet.
Show the solution
One square foot is 144 in2144 in2, so the area is 4320÷144=304320÷144=30​. Dividing by 1212 once gives 360360, which is not an area in square feet.
Practice
A planter holds 2 cubic yards of soil, and 1 yd=3 ft1 yd=3 ft. Enter the volume of that soil in cubic feet.
Show the solution
One cubic yard is 3 ft×3 ft×3 ft=27 ft33 ft×3 ft×3 ft=27 ft3, so the volume is 2×27=542×27=54​. The factor between cubic yards and cubic feet is 33=2733=27, not 33, since a volume is a product of three lengths.
Practice
Paint costs 38 dollars per can, and one can covers 25 square meters of wall. A job needs 300 square meters of wall painted. Enter the cost of the paint for that job, in dollars.
Show the solution
Cancelling square meters and then cans in 300 m2×1 can25 m2×38 dollars1 can300 m2×25 m21 can​×1 can38 dollars​ leaves 12×3812×38, so the cost in dollars is 456456​. The unit cans sits above the bar in one factor and below it in the next, so it divides out and dollars is the only unit left.
Practice
A carpenter is paid 26 dollars per hour and works 4 hours per session, and has earned 1560 dollars from those sessions alone. Enter the number of sessions worked.
Show the solution
1560 dollars×1 h26 dollars×1 session4 h1560 dollars×26 dollars1 h​×4 h1 session​ cancels dollars and hours and leaves 156026×426×41560​, so the number of sessions is 1515​. Both stated rates go in upside down from how they are written, because the chain runs from dollars back to sessions.
Practice
Each team at a school has 6 students, each bus carries 4 teams, and the school fills 9 buses for a meet. Enter the number of students the school sends.
Show the solution
Chaining the two rates gives 9 buses×4 teams1 bus×6 students1 team9 buses×1 bus4 teams​×1 team6 students​, and buses and teams cancel to leave 9×4×6=2169×4×6=216​. Per bus that is 4×6=244×6=24 students, and 9×24=2169×24=216.
Practice
On a game map, 1 span=9 notches1 span=9 notches, 4 notches=3 pips4 notches=3 pips and 1 pip=20 steps1 pip=20 steps. A road is 8 spans long. Enter its length in steps.
Show the solution
Chaining the three factors leaves 8×9×3×20448×9×3×20​, so the length in steps is 10801080​. The middle factor is 3 pips4 notches4 notches3 pips​, with notches in the denominator to cancel the 7272 notches from the first step. The flipped factor 4 notches3 pips3 pips4 notches​ gives 19201920 instead.
